### CVE-2013-0268
- Assigner: redhat | Published: 2013-02-18 | Updated: 2024-08-06 | Max CVSS: None
- CWE: n/a
- Exploit-DB 27297: Linux Kernel 3.7.6 (RedHat x86/x64) - 'MSR' Driver Privilege Escalation (local/linux, 2013-08-02, verified=0)

The msr_open function in arch/x86/kernel/msr.c in the Linux kernel before 3.7.6 allows local users to bypass intended capability restrictions by executing a crafted application as root, as demonstrated by msr32.c.

### CVE-2013-1773
- Assigner: redhat | Published: 2013-02-28 | Updated: 2024-08-06 | Max CVSS: None
- CWE: n/a
- Exploit-DB 23248: Google Android Kernel 2.6 - Local Denial of Service Crash (PoC) (dos/android, 2012-12-09, verified=1)

Buffer overflow in the VFAT filesystem implementation in the Linux kernel before 3.3 allows local users to gain privileges or cause a denial of service (system crash) via a VFAT write operation on a filesystem with the utf8 mount option, which is not properly handled during UTF-8 to UTF-16 conversion.

### CVE-2013-1828
- Assigner: redhat | Published: 2013-03-22 | Updated: 2024-08-06 | Max CVSS: None
- CWE: n/a
- Exploit-DB 24747: Linux Kernel - 'SCTP_GET_ASSOC_STATS()' Stack Buffer Overflow (PoC) (dos/linux, 2013-03-13, verified=0)

The sctp_getsockopt_assoc_stats function in net/sctp/socket.c in the Linux kernel before 3.8.4 does not validate a size value before proceeding to a copy_from_user operation, which allows local users to gain privileges via a crafted application that contains an SCTP_GET_ASSOC_STATS getsockopt system call.

### CVE-2013-1959
- Assigner: redhat | Published: 2013-05-03 | Updated: 2024-08-06 | Max CVSS: None
- CWE: n/a
- Exploit-DB 25450: Linux Kernel < 3.8.x - open-time Capability 'file_ns_capable()' Local Privilege Escalation (local/linux, 2013-05-14, verified=0)

### CVE-2013-2596
- Assigner: mitre | Published: 2013-04-13 | Updated: 2025-10-22 | Max CVSS: 7.8
- CWE: n/a; CWE-190 CWE-190 Integer Overflow or Wraparound
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 7.8 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=active, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total
- **CISA KEV**: added 2022-09-15, ransomware=Unknown — Linux Kernel Integer Overflow Vulnerability

Integer overflow in the fb_mmap function in drivers/video/fbmem.c in the Linux kernel before 3.8.9, as used in a certain Motorola build of Android 4.1.2 and other products, allows local users to create a read-write memory mapping for the entirety of kernel memory, and consequently gain privileges, via crafted /dev/graphics/fb0 mmap2 system calls, as demonstrated by the Motochopper pwn program.

- Exploit-DB 38465: Linux Kernel 3.2.1 - Tracing Multiple Local Denial of Service Vulnerabilities (dos/linux, 2013-04-15, verified=1)

### CVE-2013-4579
- Assigner: redhat | Published: 2013-11-19 | Updated: 2024-08-06 | Max CVSS: None
- CWE: n/a
- Exploit-DB 38826: Linux Kernel 3.0.5 - 'ath9k_htc_set_bssid_mask()' Information Disclosure (remote/linux, 2013-12-10, verified=1)

The ath9k_htc_set_bssid_mask function in drivers/net/wireless/ath/ath9k/htc_drv_main.c in the Linux kernel through 3.12 uses a BSSID masking approach to determine the set of MAC addresses on which a Wi-Fi device is listening, which allows remote attackers to discover the original MAC address after spoofing by sending a series of packets to MAC addresses with certain bit manipulations.

- Exploit-DB 40975: Google Android - get_user/put_user (Metasploit) (local/android, 2016-12-29, verified=1)
- Exploit-DB 31574: Linux Kernel < 3.4.5 (Android 4.2.2/4.4 ARM) - Local Privilege Escalation (local/arm, 2014-02-11, verified=0)

The (1) get_user and (2) put_user API functions in the Linux kernel before 3.5.5 on the v6k and v7 ARM platforms do not validate certain addresses, which allows attackers to read or modify the contents of arbitrary kernel memory locations via a crafted application, as exploited in the wild against Android devices in October and November 2013.
